trade-once.help: Run one strategy evaluation and, if actionable, attempt one order through the full safety pipeline. DRY-RUN unless --live is passed. Not a daemon — runs one round and exits

args.name: --symbol
args.help: Futures symbol, e.g. BTCUSDT

args.name: --interval
args.help: Timeframe interval

args.name: --strategy
args.help: Registered strategy key

args.name: --live
args.help: Actually submit the order (POST /fapi/v1/order). Without this flag, stops after showing the decision — no order-submission network call at all

run.help: Run the bots with no window until told to stop (SIGTERM, Ctrl-C; Ctrl-Break on Windows). Refuses with exit 3 if another copy holds the data root; runs the pre-flight first (exit 4, 5 or 6 on a failure). Writes a health line and state/health.json every --health-interval. Not supported for unattended money until EPIC-036B, 036C and 036E have shipped

args.name: --stop-timeout
args.help: Seconds the stop policy may take after the first signal; the whole stop may take this plus 30 (a second signal does not wait). A service unit's TimeoutStopSec must be larger than that sum

args.name: --health-interval
args.help: Seconds between health lines and snapshots

args.name: --on-stop
args.help: What stopping does to the bots: leave-orders (default) closes the workers and leaves resting orders on the exchange; stop-bots stops each active bot first (cancels its orders), for maintenance

args.name: --start-planned
args.help: Start the bots whose applied plan (bot apply) says running and that are at rest. Refused with exit 5, before anything boots, when no plan was applied or the record cannot be read

args.name: --resume-recovering
args.help: Open the order session of each venue holding a RECOVERING bot, which reconciles it with the exchange. Refused (exit 5) unless an alert channel carries bot events or --i-accept-silent-failures is given

args.name: --i-accept-silent-failures
args.help: Acknowledge that no alert channel tells you if a bot halts, so --resume-recovering may be used anyway

args.name: --confirm-venue
args.help: Type the mainnet venue to allow real-money bots to be started or resumed on it (--start-planned, --resume-recovering). Without it --start-planned and --resume-recovering are refused (exit 2) when they would touch a mainnet venue

args.name: --skip-preflight
args.help: Do not run the pre-flight before serving. Logged as a WARNING; the key, the clock and the exchange are then not checked

args.name: --host-signal
args.help: Tell a service manager the host is ready, alive and stopping. sdnotify is for a systemd Type=notify unit on Linux and does not work in a container without its NOTIFY_SOCKET

status.help: Say whether a host is running and what it holds. Exit 0 running, 10 not running, 11 running but unhealthy

args.name: --json
args.help: Print the result as JSON (schema sew.status/1) instead of the text report

args.name: --format
args.help: Output format: text (default), json, or any other registered format

args.name: --watch
args.help: Repeat the report until Ctrl-C

args.name: --interval
args.help: Seconds between reports with --watch

args.name: --format

apply.help: Make the bots match a plan file: create, edit and (with --prune) delete bots through the commands the Bots tab uses, and record each entry's desired_state for run --start-planned. Applying starts and stops nothing. A second apply of the same plan changes nothing

args.name: plan
args.help: The plan file (JSON, schema sew.bot-plan/1); it holds no key, secret or account identifier

args.name: --dry-run
args.help: Print what would change and change nothing; works beside a running host

args.name: --prune
args.help: Also delete the stored bots the plan does not name, if they are at rest (DRAFT or STOPPED); a rename is a delete and a create

args.name: --json
args.help: Print the result as JSON (schema sew.bot-apply/1) instead of the text report

args.name: --format
args.help: Output format: text (default), json, or any other registered format

export.help: Write a plan file from the stored bots (never overwrites a file); apply --dry-run of it then reports no changes

args.name: --all
args.help: Export every bot

args.name: --bot-id
args.help: Export one bot (see bot list)

args.name: --output
args.help: The plan file to create; it must not exist yet

args.name: --json
args.help: Print the result as JSON (schema sew.bot-export/1) instead of the text report

args.name: --format
